evidence: The mutable-ref fact is true but the escalation framing is not: the called workflow declares permissions: contents: write and a reusable workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN cannot exceed the caller's, which this same file already grants, so pinning buys no privilege reduction here. The agent's compensating claim checks out - gh api repos/promptctl/.github/branches/master/protection returns enforce_admins enabled, allow_force_pushes false and required_pull_request_reviews present - though required_approving_review_count is 0, so PR-only does not actually guarantee a second reader; against a same-owner org repo the residual risk is small and a per-repo SHA pin would genuinely re-create the N-copy drift this PR exists to delete.
guidance_note: When adopting an external ref, put the pinning decision and its compensating control in the workflow file's own header comment so the choice is visible to review instead of being re-litigated in a thread.

evidence: README.md at the PR's first commit 249d2c3 still read 'runs on every push to master ... To cut a release: bump the version in the plugin's plugin.json, merge to master, and the workflow does the rest', while release.yml in that same commit triggers only on tags ['*--v*'] - a maintainer following it would have waited for a release that never fires. Fixed in daf8d07.
guidance_note: When a commit deletes a mechanism, grep the repo's prose for descriptions of that mechanism and update them in the same commit rather than leaving the docs to a later round.

evidence: The paragraph daf8d07 wrote restated the tag shape {name}--v{version}, the exact command claude plugin tag <plugin-dir> --push, and the workflow's validation - all three verbatim facts of promptctl/.github's RELEASING.md, which I read - so the F2 fix replaced stale local prose with a fresh cross-repo duplicate, contradicting the header comment the same PR added to release.yml saying this repo only says when it runs. ec275e2 cut it to a link plus that one owned fact.
guidance_note: When a fix moves a procedure's home to a shared document, the local doc gets the link plus only the facts this repo owns; restating the moved steps re-creates the duplication the move was for.

evidence: At 249d2c3 the README said 'Three skills, version 0.1.0' (line 42) and 'Version 0.1.0.' (line 93) while both plugin.json manifests already read 0.1.2 and the CHANGELOGs this PR adds start at v0.1.2 - so the staleness is pre-existing text no fix commit touched, and the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is causally about scope, not content: README.md entered the diff only through the F2 fix, which is why round 2 read the whole file. Same doc-versus-manifest staleness class the F2/F3 edits did not sweep; 783be75 deleted both numbers.
guidance_note: When a fix pulls a previously-untouched file into the diff, sweep that whole file for the same class of staleness before pushing, because the next round will read all of it, not just the edited section.

narrative: A 4-round, +42/-99 CI-plumbing PR where every round after the first was bought by the documentation fix, not by the code. Round 0 raised one architectural objection the agent correctly declined with a verified compensating control (F1) and one true doc-staleness finding (F2). The F2 fix rewrote the README Releases section as a summary of the external RELEASING.md, which round 1 flagged as fresh cross-repo duplication (F3); trimming that to a pointer left README.md in the diff, and round 2 then read the rest of the file and found two pre-existing 'version 0.1.0' claims contradicting the 0.1.2 manifests (F4). Both extra rounds were avoidable by a single wider pass over README.md at the moment the file was first opened.
guidance_observations: Editing a file for the first time during review expands the reviewer's scope to the whole file, so the first edit should be preceded by a full-file staleness pass, not a section-local one.

Documentation fixes were the entire cost of this PR's extra rounds while the one code-shaped finding was settled in a single exchange, which suggests doc-consistency checks belong in the pre-push routine rather than the review loop.
The one pushback was strengthened by a checkable external fact (branch protection on the shared repo) rather than by the law citation alone, and it closed in one round because of it.
